mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not lead to negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month does not lead to negative 5-day forward returns in > 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases do not correlate with positive 60-day forward returns (correlation coefficient < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM does not lead to negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 2% and GDPC1 growth < 2% does not lead to negative 60-day forward returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month does not lead to positive 5-day forward returns in > 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases do not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns (correlation coefficient < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) is decreasing and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is increasing, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the interaction of decreasing INDPRO and increasing UNRATE does not lead to negative 60-day forward returns in > 60% of instances.
